stories.headline: WMAS crews lost 32,810 hours outside hospitals
stories.body: West Midlands Ambulance Service told its board that in September only 28.5% of handovers were done within 15 minutes and 22.7% took over an hour. Category 2 response times have improved.
stories.why: Hours at hospital are hours not responding. The trust warned patient harm is "undoubtedly happening".

stories.headline: LAS and EMAS brace for a busy Halloween weekend
stories.body: LAS says Category 1 calls have climbed to around 480 a day, against about 400 on a typical busy day. EMAS is adding extra crews and vehicles after 3,865 calls last Halloween, versus about 3,400 on a normal day.
stories.why: Halloween and Bonfire Night fall within a week of each other, so expect busier shifts across both.

stories.headline: Ambulance CEO warns sector isn't ready for terror attack
stories.body: A chief executive who has led ambulance trusts for 23 years has warned the sector is not "sufficiently trained, equipped, or resourced" to respond to a terrorist attack.
stories.why: Major incident readiness affects every crew. It's worth knowing your trust's plans and your role in them.

stories.headline: Contract to train hundreds of SWASFT support workers
stories.body: Training provider MediPro has won a contract to train hundreds of Level 3 Ambulance Support Worker (Emergency) apprentices for South Western Ambulance Service, starting January 2027.
stories.why: More support workers means more crewing capacity, though some providers have closed amid sector cuts.

stories.headline: Baby born in an ambulance on the A96
stories.body: A Moray mum gave birth in the back of an ambulance between Elgin and Aberdeen, with a paramedic helping. Consultant-led maternity at her local hospital has been downgraded since 2018.
stories.why: Long rural transfers mean emergency birth skills can be needed on any shift.
